section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch1 — Research Methods in Child Development
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A researcher studies the SAME group of 50 children, testing their vocabulary every year from age 3 to age 10, tracking how each child's language develops over time. This research design is called the:
explanation: The longitudinal method studies the SAME individuals repeatedly over an extended time period, revealing genuine developmental change within individuals.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch1 — Research Methods in Child Development
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A researcher, wanting quicker results, instead studies DIFFERENT groups of children aged 3, 5, 7, and 10 all at the same time, comparing their vocabulary levels to infer a developmental trend. This research design is called the:
explanation: The cross-sectional method compares DIFFERENT age groups at a single point in time — faster but risks confusing true developmental change with cohort differences.
